issues.description: Problem statement requires SealSaloon to have a non-static final Stock field ("final Stock stock" initialized in the constructor), but later explicitly states the stock attribute must be static and shared across all instances. The solution follows the latter (static final stock). This contradiction makes it unclear to students whether stock is instance-specific or shared.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (A) update Part 1 text and UML to declare `private static final Stock stock` (and remove mention of constructor initialization for stock), or (B) remove the requirement that stock/acceptSupplyDelivery/calculateTotalPrice are static and adjust solution/tests accordingly.

issues.description: Template Stock.getStockIngredients() returns List<StockIngredient>, but the solution changes it to return StockIngredient[]. Students implementing according to the template may end up with an API incompatible with the reference solution/tests that expect an array (also aligns with UML multiplicity as an array-like field).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the API: either change the template to `public StockIngredient[] getStockIngredients()` (matching solution) or change the solution to return `List<StockIngredient>` and update any dependent code/tests. Prefer array return type to match existing internal representation and UML.

issues.description: The UML/spec asks to 'add getters for all private fields'. In the solution, SealSaloon provides `public static Stock getStock()` (static getter), whereas the template Main (commented) uses `shop.getStock()` suggesting an instance method call. Static methods can be called via an instance in Java but this is confusing and contradicts the 'final Stock stock' (instance field) described earlier.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify getter semantics consistent with the chosen stock design: if stock is static, mention in the statement that `getStock()` is static (and use `SealSaloon.getStock()` in examples); if stock is per-instance, make `getStock()` an instance method returning the instance field.

issues.description: The Stock getter for the stock inventory is named differently between template and solution: template exposes getStockIngredients() returning a List<StockIngredient>, while solution exposes getStockIngredients() returning StockIngredient[]. Same conceptual entity (the stockIngredients collection) but different API shape and implied identifier meaning (list vs array), which can confuse students when mapping requirements (array-based operations) to the provided starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make Stock.getStockIngredients() consistent across template and solution by using the same return type and representation (prefer StockIngredient[] as described by the diagram). If a List view is desired, add an additional method like getStockIngredientsList() rather than changing getStockIngredients().
